name: orkestr Sandboxes

modes.label: Pay-as-you-go sandbox (metered on actual use)
modes.note: orkestr.eu/pricing (Sandboxes tab, JS bundle, 2026-09-28): vCPU EUR 0.045/hour, RAM EUR 0.015/GiB-hour, storage EUR 0.10/GB-month; sizes small 1 vCPU/1 GB, medium 2 vCPU/4 GB, large 4 vCPU/8 GB ('cost shown at full utilization'). Metered 'per second, on actual usage - real on-CPU time and working-set RAM, not the provisioned size'. Converted at 1.1378 USD/EUR (ECB 2026-09-28). Prices in EUR, VAT applied where required.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: No card: 'EUR 5 credit, then it stops', 'Small only, 3 concurrent', '30-min sessions'. Trial only.

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Card on file: 'EUR 25 credit, then metered', all sizes, concurrency 'High' (number not published), sessions 'Up to 24 h', 10 snapshots, own spend cap.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Dedicated EU nodes, custom limits + SLA, audit logs, SSO. Custom price.

caveats: Rates come from the Sandboxes tab of orkestr.eu/pricing (rendered from the site's JS bundle); the orkestr.eu/sandboxes page still says 'Published rates land once we have metered real workloads'. Treat as a published but early (beta) rate card. Billed on actual on-CPU time and working-set RAM, so idle sandboxes cost almost nothing. First 10 GB of held storage (snapshots + templates) free, then EUR 0.10/GB-month. Egress price unpublished; full egress needs a paid verified account.
Default network off; full egress needs paid verified account.
150–300 ms cold-start claims vary by page/template; no benchmark recorded.
Worked example assumes resources are released between active windows unless a retained-instance scenario is explicitly discussed.
VAT basis: Unknown: reviewed pricing source does not explicitly establish VAT/tax inclusion.
Residency: Provider claims code, memory, snapshots and environment remain EU; Falkenstein DE, Helsinki FI, Roubaix FR; DPA available. Not independently audited.

Billing-basis conflict: the pricing FAQ says sandboxes bill actual on-CPU time and working-set RAM (idle almost free), but orkestr.eu/docs/sandboxes says each sandbox is 'metered per second of wall-clock time it's alive (whether or not the workload is busy)'. Idle-heavy estimates may be understated until the provider resolves this.

fleet.verification: Verified email earns starter credit, no card; card unlocks all sandbox sizes and paid metering.
fleet.notes: Sandbox PAYG is independent of Platform subscription. Platform PR-preview concurrent deployments (1/5) are not Sandbox runtime quotas. No numeric new-account sandbox count or increase path found.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: on_timeout	string	What happens at the deadline: kill (default) terminates the sandbox; pause snapshots it so a later /resume continues where it left off.
snapshot_auto.note: Opt-in per sandbox at create (on_timeout=pause; default is kill). Triggered by the lifetime deadline; snapshot captures memory + disk (running processes resume). Pairs with auto_resume=true, which resumes automatically on the next exec/file call or preview-URL HTTP request. Free tier falls back to terminate when at its snapshot cap (1).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/pause snapshots the sandbox and stops the compute meter. ... POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/resume restores from the most recent snapshot for that sandbox. ... The snapshot is consumed by the resume - pause again to take a new one
snapshot_on_demand.note: On-demand snapshot is pause-style: memory + disk captured (security page: 'the VM's memory and disk state are captured into a snapshot'), sandbox is suspended, and the snapshot is single-use, restoring the same sandbox only. No fork / boot-new-machines-from-snapshot documented; custom templates are built from a base image + recipe, not captured from a running sandbox. Retention 7 d free / 30 d carded / no expiry enterprise.

harness_api.quote:
result = sbx.exec(
    'npx claude -p "Run the test suite and fix the first failing test" '
    "--output-format json --dangerously-skip-permissions",
harness_api.note: The official Claude Code guide drives the agent through the generic exec API (npm install, then claude -p / --resume via exec); no dedicated harness API. Separately, orkestr 'Workers' (preview) run orkestr's own ops agent on its hosted runtime with your model key (objective, skills, memory, approvals, run transcripts), but that is a platform-ops agent product, not a harness API for sandboxes.

egress_allowlist.quote: When you pass allow_domains, those domains become the entire allowlist for that sandbox.
egress_allowlist.note: Three modes per sandbox: off (default, no network device), restricted (HTTPS-only forward proxy with curated default allowlist or custom allow_domains; no raw sockets/DNS), open. Enforced by a provider-side proxy; allowlist can be baked into a template. Hostname-level only; 'Custom egress allowlist: yes' on all tiers (limits page), though API ref says '(paid plans)'.

egress_http_rules.quote: Entries are bare hostnames - no scheme, port, path or wildcard.
egress_http_rules.note: Allowlist is hostname-only (HTTPS port 443); no method/path/header rules documented.

ingress_rules.quote: Pass preview_auth=True at create (previewAuth: true in JS) and the sandbox's preview URLs stop being public: every request must carry the minted preview_auth_token or the edge returns 401.
ingress_rules.note: Ports are exposed per port via get_host(port) at <port>-<id>.sbx.orkestr.run; public (unguessable URL) by default, token-gated with preview_auth. Needs networked mode + card on file. No IP allowlists documented.

guest_firewall.note: Each sandbox is its own VM with its own kernel ('not a container sharing a host kernel'); recipe steps run as root and apt-get works at run time, so root is available. Egress policy is enforced outside the VM regardless (off = no NIC; restricted = proxy).

secret_proxy.quote: Secrets you inject (as env vars or files) are visible to whatever code runs in that sandbox - including code a model wrote.
secret_proxy.note: Sandbox secrets are env vars/files inside the VM (kept in memory, persisted inside pause snapshots). The Claude Code guide passes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as an env var. (Workers product keeps git credentials in the control plane, but that is not a sandbox egress proxy.)

volume_attach.quote: A persistent volume is a named disk that survives a sandbox and follows you to the next one. Attach it and it mounts at /persist
volume_attach.note: ext4 disk local to the host, checkpointed to EU object storage; default 10 GB, max 100 GB per volume; 1/10/50 volumes and 10 GB/200 GB/2 TB total per tier; billed GB-month on provisioned size; optional max_lifetime auto-destroy.

volume_shared.quote: A volume can back only one running (or paused) sandbox at a time. Attaching a volume that's already in use returns a 409 volume_in_use
volume_shared.note: Single writer by design (ext4 RW); no read-only multi-attach or shared FS documented.
